audio.t: Good evening, everyone. I'm Officer Lin from the Campus Security Office. I'm here tonight because the number of bicycle accidents on campus has nearly doubled since last year. Most of them happen on the slope near the library, especially in the evening when students are rushing to class.

So, starting next month, we're introducing a few new rules. First, the speed limit for bikes and scooters on campus will be fifteen kilometers per hour. Second, riding while using your phone, even just to check a map, will result in a warning the first time and a fine of three hundred dollars after that. And third, all bikes must have a working front light after six p.m.

We know these rules may feel strict, but our goal isn't to punish anyone. In fact, this Friday from noon to four, we'll be giving out free bike lights in front of the Student Center. Just bring your student ID. If you have any questions, you can email our office or stop by our booth on Friday.

questions.explain: 林警官開頭說校內腳踏車事故比去年幾乎倍增，因此來說明，故選 C。接駁車、招募志工、失竊皆未提及。

To recruit student safety volunteers
Because bicycle accidents have increased
Because many bikes have been stolen

head: From: General Affairs Office
To: All Students
Subject: Removal of Abandoned Bicycles
passage: Every semester, hundreds of bicycles are left unused in campus parking areas, taking up space that other riders need. To keep our bike racks available, the General Affairs Office will remove abandoned bicycles from all campus parking areas on December 3.

Between now and November 27, staff will attach yellow tags to bicycles that appear to have been abandoned, such as those with flat tires, rusty chains, or no lock. If your bike has been tagged but you still use it, simply tear off the tag. Bikes that still have a tag on December 3 will be moved to the storage area behind the Physical Education Building.
Removed bikes can be **reclaimed** until December 31 with a valid student ID. After that, they will be repaired by student volunteers and donated to new international students.
Thank you for helping keep our campus tidy.

questions.explain: 信中說明 12 月 3 日將清除校內廢棄腳踏車，故選 D。信中沒有販售或收費；志工修車只是後續處理，並非寫信目的。
options: To advertise used bicycles for sale
To introduce a new bicycle parking fee
To ask for volunteers to repair bikes
To announce the removal of unused bicycles
questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the email?

passage: Last Wednesday, the university announced a three-year plan to make the campus safer and greener by reducing the number of cars on its roads. Under the plan, the large parking lot next to the main gate will gradually be turned into a green space with seating areas, and visitor parking will be moved to a new underground garage on the edge of campus.

The decision follows a survey conducted last spring by the Student Association. Of the more than two thousand students who responded, sixty-two percent said they felt unsafe walking on campus during busy hours, and nearly half reported having almost been hit by a car or scooter at least once. "These roads were designed decades ago, when far fewer people came to campus," explained Professor Chen Wei-ting of the Department of Urban Planning, who helped draft the plan.

To make up for the lost parking spaces, the university will add four kilometers of protected bike lanes and replace its diesel shuttle buses with electric ones. During peak hours, the shuttle will also run every ten minutes instead of every twenty.

Not everyone is pleased, however. Some staff members who commute from nearby towns worry that the changes will make their daily trips longer, especially on rainy days. "Not everyone can ride a bike for forty minutes," said one administrative assistant. In response, the university says it will offer discounted public transportation passes to employees and keep a limited number of parking spaces for people with disabilities and staff with special needs.
The first stage of the plan, the new bike lanes, is expected to be completed by next September.

questions.explain: 全文介紹學校減少校內汽車的三年交通計畫，故選 C。問卷只是計畫背景；道路歷史只是教授的一句話；文中沒有抗議或停車費。
